items.question: What is LINQ, and how do query syntax and method syntax relate?
items.answer: LINQ is a set of operators and language clauses that query any IEnumerable or IQueryable source with compile-time types. Query expressions (from/where/select) are translated by the compiler into method calls such as Where and Select. There is no performance difference from that translation. Operators without a keyword (Count, ToList, SelectMany's more exotic overloads) stay as methods. You can mix both in one statement.
followUps: Which operators have no query-syntax keyword?
Does query syntax allocate extra compared with methods?
items.sixtySeconds: Language queries over sequences. Query syntax is sugar for the same methods. Mix when a keyword does not exist.

items.question: Explain deferred execution and a hot-path bug you have seen.
items.answer: Declaring a query does not run it. Each enumeration re-executes against the current source. On an attempt-submit reporting path, a Where on a shared list that you then Count() and later foreach will see two different snapshots, and Count already walked the filter once. ToList once, then share the list. Closing over a mutable filter flag that changes between enumerations is the same class of bug. OrderBy buffers; chaining Where after OrderBy still waits until enumeration.
followUps: What does multiple enumeration of an IEnumerable from a live queue look like?
items.sixtySeconds: Plan versus run. Each foreach re-runs. ToList to freeze. Count then foreach is two passes.

items.question: IEnumerable versus IQueryable — what actually differs?
items.answer: IEnumerable operators take Func delegates and run in process (LINQ to Objects). IQueryable operators take Expression<Func<...>> trees. A provider may rewrite the tree to SQL, to a search DSL, or it may throw. Calling AsQueryable on a List<T> still executes with Enumerable after a thin wrapper — it is not a database. Interview level stops here: know that statement lambdas, local functions, and many newer C# features are not in expression trees. This track does not teach Entity Framework Core mapping.
followUps: What happens if you call ToList in the middle of an IQueryable chain?
Why might a provider throw on a custom instance method in a Where?
items.sixtySeconds: Delegates in memory versus expression trees for a provider. AsQueryable on a list is still in-memory.

items.question: What does SelectMany buy you that Select does not?
items.answer: Select maps one-to-one. SelectMany maps one-to-many and concatenates. Nested from clauses, flattening attempt.Answers per exam, and joining a jagged CSV line into cells are SelectMany. The result length is the sum of inner lengths, not the outer count. Interviewers use it to see if you confuse it with Select of a collection that you then nest-foreach.
followUps: How do you keep the outer element while flattening?
items.sixtySeconds: SelectMany flattens. Two from clauses. Length is sum of inners.
